summary: Submitted the direct check for unit-C-snapshot-install-log-identity (action=check). Plan (checks/plan.json) and harness (checks/assurance_generated_test.go) drive real target code: a follower with a monotonic LogStore and a cached last log index of 5 handles a real InstallSnapshot at index 2 through the real installSnapshot handler (the real FSM goroutine performs the restore step with a no-op stub FSM), then receives the appendEntries request the leader would send from the snapshot index. Prerequisites are snapshot_installed (node n1, success true) and post_install_identity (node n1), and the monitor observes recovery_probe on the same stream with oracle accepted==true and identity node, so a rejection after a successful install is a complete violating witness for the bounded recovery responsibility. Construction guidance from a scratch copy of the captured source (draft/tmp/raftbuild, offline module cache) showed the store emptied to last index 0 while the cached identity and getLastEntry stayed at index 5, and the follow-up request rejected; that local run is construction knowledge only and formal evidence requires the trusted runner's clean-copy execution. Legality grounding cites S-raft-installsnapshot/S-logstore-monotonic/S-raft-appendentries and the binding BND-install-snapshot-reset-logs; the plan records the honest semantic changes (skipStartup with only the FSM goroutine, directly installed single-voter configuration, arbitrary snapshot bytes with matching Size, stub FSM) plus uncertainties (single follower, no cluster consequence, monotonic branch only). Preflight returned valid:true; the two earlier findings remain confirmed.
